projects.title: Sci-fi world
projects.articleBody:
Since watching Project Hail Mary I've quite liked a minimalist approach to space worldbuilding :3

Technology

Early-stage, grungy space-faring sci-fi setting — no crazy advanced technologies like teleportation or forcefields, or cool, clean, aesthetic technologies like holograms or FTL. Long-haul interplanetary space freighters with thousands of crew travelling are the primary means of travelling through deep space.

Solar system

Mercury is being mined out for iron and stuff.

Mettra is a captured rogue planet with a highly eccentric orbit. It is the homeworld of the exceedingly hardy mettra, an alien species that take the appearance of blue-skinned feminine humanoids with pointed ears. Mettra's gravity is significantly higher than Earth's, promoting higher muscle and bone density that allows mettra to achieve inhuman weight gain; as a result, mettra are exceedingly stockier and bulkier than any human. Mettra are able to communicate telepathically with other mettra at any distance instantaneously (specifically, without first encoding the idea into language), an ability subject to continued scientific inquiry. Mettra are culturally distinct, with many formal behaviours humans would consider immodest.

Vordokt is a Venusian moon of Mettra with an incredibly dense atmosphere. It harbors non-sapient extremophiles.

Degbora is a habitable, Earth-like moon of Mettra, and the only non-Earth celestial body permanently inhabited by humans insofar.

Leylines are streams of plasma that course throughout the solar system, around which have occurred the only recorded sightings of angels, mysterious beings of pure energy. Angels materialize by manipulating plasma into a humanoid shape, but continue to exist without doing so (when they aren't occupying matter, they don't take up space nor have a 'position'; they exist everywhere within the universe at once). Angels are described by the few who've seen their materialized form as ghostly women with long, mermaid-like tails of plasma and enormous breasts.

projects.title: Medieval dark fantasy
projects.description: flavoured with ritual magic, Remington 870s, and cute cow-girls
projects.articleBody:
Cultists are people who have been exhiled for attempting to commune with the 'old gods,' with the goal of getting the old gods to perform magic through them (preferrably both controllably and permanently, but cultists don't really care as long as something bad happens). No one actually knows what the old gods are (if there are multiple or just one, if they're simply an unconscious mechanism of the universe, or even what is necessary to do to successfully commune), but whatever they are, cultists are able to get them to cause some pretty disastrous things to happen by doing random things deep in the forest until something works.

Ten years ago today, a blight befell the land from which we have yet to recover...

I had heard this beastly shriek and doubled back across the small trek I had made; when I reached a wall I turned around and it was this sickly, toothy monster on all fours skittering my way, so I without aiming fired a shot from my rifle in its direction and it disappeared back into the fog...

The cultists worked under cover of darkness, gathering branches and stones from the forest to create an effigy to what they believed was a very, very powerful god. Similar pursuits had worked in the past, but inconsistently, and they recorded as much as they could of what they had done, the position of the stars, the fullness of their stomachs, anything; they worked obsessively to find the common factor.

The earliest records they have place the first experiments decades prior; before that, who knows. They refused to believe that it — any of it — was random; what would it say about the world that something so powerful was purely up to chance?

They burned their work before sunrise to cover their tracks.

An altar carved into the cliff-face obscured by the forest surrounding. The only indication towards its existence was the soft orange glow of the candles within, and more faintly, the blue glow of apparently nothing at all.
